pull_request.title: Preserve hunkless diff paths containing the side delimiter
pull_request.body:
For an unquoted mode-only or binary diff of a path such as `src b/nested file.bin`, Git writes `diff --git a/src b/nested file.bin b/src b/nested file.bin`. The parser's greedy side-delimiter removal consumes the ` b/` inside the new path and displays only `nested file.bin`. Such changes have no `---`/`+++` headers to recover the full name.

Recognize the exact repeated `a/name b/name` spelling before using the existing fallback. Explicit rename, text-side headers, and quoted-name handling keep their current priority. This fixes the repeated-path case; it does not claim to solve every rename/copy header ambiguity.

Validation: a local Node24 runner stripped TypeScript types from the actual parser and exercised actual Git-generated mode-only/binary patches. Both cases fail upstream and pass with the fix. The existing pure-parser fixture and new canonical regression also pass through an assertion/registration adapter (4 local tests total); the committed regression uses the existing `claude-code/testing` convention.

Native plugin validation at `753fd64b6bd378553e14d210b09fab5562c4c805` with Claude Code 2.1.316: `claude plugin validate plugins/worktrunk` passes with the existing missing-version warning, and `claude plugin test plugins/worktrunk` passes all 9 canonical tests. Restoring only the relevant production file to upstream while retaining the new canonical test gives 8 passes and 1 failure; the unchanged upstream suite passes all 8 tests. The plugin snapshots were checked against every tracked Git blob at the PR head. These local runs use the canonical mocked host events, not a live terminal/provider session. The local Rust pre-merge hook was not run; hosted status is separate from these local plugin results.

AI disclosure: code, regression test, and this description were prepared with Codex and independently reviewed by another Codex agent. No human-authorship or human-review claim is made.

comments.author: worktrunk-bot
comments.body:
With `git diff --find-copies-harder`, copying `x b/x b/x` to `x` produces `diff --git a/x b/x b/x b/x` with a `copy to x` header. This match treats it as a same-path change, so `parsePatch` now reports `x b/x` instead of the destination `x` that the previous fallback returned. Skip this shortcut for copy headers.

```suggestion
    const samePath = has('copy to ') ? undefined : /^diff --git a\/(.*) b\/\1$/.exec(first)?.[1]
```
